transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in because... lately my mind just feels really foggy. I work at the library, and I can't even keep my place in my old cataloguing notes anymore. I just sit there and... I can't seem to decide what simple thing to do next. It's just been really hard to think straight.
How long have you been experiencing this foggy thinking and difficulty concentrating?

Well, it's been about three months now. The fogginess and just... this generally low mood, they've been there most days. It seemed to really start up right around the time I began preparing to leave the library.
Over these past three months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels?

Well, my sleep has definitely been off. I go to bed feeling tired enough, but then I always seem to wake up around four in the morning. I can't get back to sleep after that... I just lie there in the dark, thinking about what I am supposed to do with myself now.
Over these past three months, have you found that things you normally enjoy doing—like hobbies or activities you used to like—just don't feel enjoyable to you anymore?

Yeah, I have. Most days lately, I just sit at the kitchen table... and it feels like the color has just gone out of everything. I used to really enjoy my old watercolor books, but now... looking at them just makes me feel heavy instead of interested. I just don't get any enjoyment out of them right now.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight, or do you feel unusually cold compared to before?

I haven't noticed feeling unusually cold, no. But as for my weight... well, it's mostly that my appetite is just gone. I actually have to remind myself to eat these days. My wife has been noticing it, too. She points out that I leave my rice and soup half-finished... and before all this, I would never waste a meal.

Besides the fatigue from your low mood, have you noticed that you feel unusually tired or sluggish even when you've had enough rest, or that your movements and thinking feel slowed down in a way that seems physical rather than just from feeling sad?

Yeah, I have noticed that. My body just feels... slow lately. It's like, even doing basic things—walking down to the corner store, or just sorting papers on my desk at work—it all takes way more effort than it should. It definitely feels physical, like my limbs are just heavy and I'm having to force myself through every movement.

Besides the fatigue and heaviness you've described, have you noticed any other changes in your body—such as your skin becoming drier, your hair falling out more than usual, or having more constipation than you did before?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My skin seems about the same, and my hair... well, it's been thinning for years, but nothing sudden. And my digestion has been fine, no issues with constipation or anything. It's really just the slowness and the lack of appetite that I've noticed physically.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, infections, or health problems in the past few months? Or has your doctor ever told you that you have thyroid problems, anemia, or other chronic conditions?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick recently, no infections or anything. And my doctor hasn't ever mentioned thyroid problems or anemia. Overall, my physical health has been pretty normal, aside from what we've just talked about.

Have you had any head injuries, falls, or blows to the head in the past few months? Or have you experienced any sudden neurological symptoms like dizziness, headaches, difficulty with balance, or any unusual sensations?

No, I haven't hit my head or taken any falls. No concussions or anything like that. And I haven't had any dizzy spells or weird headaches either. My balance is fine. It's really just the slowness I mentioned before, nothing else out of the ordinary.
